$comment: Reproducibility pins: (published npm version) -> (commit whose build produces its exact dist bytes).
This is the evidence base for scripts/check-publish-drift.mjs. That detector's whole authority is
the claim 'this repo's dist output is byte-reproducible', because npm exposes no gitHead for these
packages. A claim the gate never re-tests is a phantom mechanism, so publish-drift.yml rebuilds a
pinned commit on every run and asserts --expect-in-sync before any drift verdict is trusted.
Add a new pin each time a version is published, in the release PR.
Every pin declares a status: 'verified' means its rebuild was compared byte-for-byte against the
published tarballs on the verifiedAt date; 'pending' means not yet re-proven and is ignored.
Which pin the gate rebuilds is chosen semantically by scripts/resolve-release-pin.mjs — the newest
verified pin, by version. Position in this array carries no authority: reordering these entries
cannot change the selection, and appending a pending pin cannot hijack it.
This file must stay in canonical JSON form (2-space indent, trailing newline, no duplicate keys); the resolver fails closed otherwise and prints the one-liner that rewrites it.
